lines: Taylor Nguyen
+1 (555) 010-6642 | taylor.nguyen@example.com | example.com/code/tnguyen
EDUCATION
Westfield State University | M.S. in Computer Science | Metro City, USA | Sep 2024 - Expected Jun 2026
Westfield State University | B.S. in Computer Science | Metro City, USA | Sep 2019 - Jun 2023
EXPERIENCE
Lumen Travel | Frontend Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2025 - Sep 2025
- Rebuilt the hotel search results page in React with server-side rendering, cutting median load time from 3.8s to 1.6s and raising bookings per search 9% in an A/B test.
- Cut the booking flow's JavaScript from 410 KB to 260 KB by code-splitting the calendar and map widgets.
- Added keyboard navigation and screen-reader labels to the date picker, fixing all 14 accessibility issues flagged in the audit.
- Moving image resizing to the CDN, inlining critical CSS, preloading the two web fonts and deferring the analytics script, raised the checkout page's Lighthouse performance score from 52 to 91.
- Cut the landing page's largest contentful paint from 4.1s to 1.2s by adding loading="lazy" to the hero image.
- Documented the design-system tokens in Storybook so designers could check spacing and color values without asking engineers.
Westfield State University | Web Developer, IT Services | Metro City, USA | Apr 2024 - Aug 2024
- Cut the university sites' JavaScript bundle by 60% by converting their PNG images to WebP.
- Interviewed 8 department editors about publishing; the findings led to a preview mode that cut broken pages reported by students from 30 to 6 a month.
- Writes the accessibility checklist for all university web pages, reducing failed audits from 12 to 2 a semester.
- Rebuilt the course-catalog search with client-side filtering, cutting search time from 4 seconds to under 1.
PROJECTS
Transit Arrival Web App | Independent Project | TypeScript, React | Oct 2025 - Present
- Built a progressive web app showing live bus arrivals for 400 stops, used by about 900 riders a week.
- Cut cold-start time on slow 3G from 3.0s to 1.5s, a 75% improvement, by caching the stop list offline.
- Raised weekly returning riders by 10% in the first month, from 30% to 40%, by adding saved stops.
Library Room Booking | Hackathon, Team of 4 | Vue | Feb 2024 - Mar 2024
- Worked on the frontend of the booking flow using React and TypeScript.
- Wrote the booking calendar component and its tests, handling overlapping bookings and time-zone changes.
- Presented the demo to the library staff and handed over the code with setup notes.
SKILLS
Tools: TypeScript, React, Vue, Storybok, Angular
Methods: server-side rendering, accessibility, component testing

items.says: Replace any placeholder contact details or portfolio link before applying.
items.because: The contact details should work, and the link should load and show relevant work.

items.says: Define “load time” and explain how it was collected.
items.because: The measure behind the reported reduction is unclear.

items.says: Substantiate the 9% booking result with A/B-test details.
items.because: Without the duration, sample size, and statistical reliability, readers may interpret the figure as stronger evidence than it is.

items.says: Specify what the KB figures represent and how they were measured.
items.because: The comparison needs to be like-for-like.

items.says: Clarify the audit’s scope and your contribution to the 14 fixes.
items.because: “All” is a strong claim that the findings and completed work need to support.

items.says: Make the bullet’s timing and ownership clearer.
items.because: The opening construction makes them less clear.

items.says: Keep the verb tense consistent with the other bullets.
Explain the test conditions behind the Lighthouse scores.
items.because: Scores can vary with the environment.

items.says: Recheck the claim that lazy-loading the hero image caused the LCP improvement.
items.because: Lazy-loading a hero image visible immediately can delay LCP.

items.says: Make the scope of the Storybook documentation more concrete.
items.because: The current benefit is understandable but difficult to assess.

items.says: The bullet attributes a JavaScript-bundle reduction to PNG-to-WebP conversion.
items.because: Converting image formats normally reduces image bytes, not JavaScript bundle size.

items.says: Clarify the period and source of the monthly broken-page counts.
Clarify how preview mode relates to the reduction in broken pages.
Change “Writes” to match the completed role’s tense.
items.because: The role has ended.

items.says: Verify that the checklist applied to all university pages.
items.because: “All university web pages” is a broad claim.

items.says: Check that the audit-failure figures use comparable criteria and periods.
Define what “search time” measures.
items.because: The numbers could describe time to results, interaction latency, or a measured user task.

items.says: Substantiate the 400-stop and 900-weekly-rider figures.
items.because: Real usage of an independent project is a standout claim likely to draw follow-up questions.

items.says: Clarify whether the app was publicly deployed and how usage was counted.
The stated 75% improvement is incorrect.
items.because: A reduction from 3.0 seconds to 1.5 seconds is 50%.

items.says: Define “cold-start” and explain how the slow-3G measurement was run.
Clarify how offline caching produced the reported cold-start improvement.
items.because: Caching may help later or offline visits rather than a truly uncached first load.

items.says: The change from 30% to 40% is presented as a 10% increase.
items.because: It is a 10-percentage-point increase, which could be mistaken for a 10% relative increase.

items.says: Explain the denominator and measurement period for returning riders.
Support the claim that saved stops caused the change.
The React and TypeScript bullet conflicts with the project heading’s Vue listing.
items.because: A reviewer may read the framework mismatch as a factual inconsistency.

items.says: Clarify what you implemented personally rather than what the team built.
Verify that the listed edge cases were tested and explain the tests’ scope.
items.because: “Wrote the tests” is stronger when their scope is clear.

items.says: Prioritize evidence of your contribution or the project’s result over handoff details if space is tight.
items.because: The demo and handoff are less informative than the other project bullets.

items.says: “Storybok” is misspelled.
items.because: It should be “Storybook.”

items.says: Keep Angular only if you can discuss your experience with it.
items.because: Otherwise, it may invite questions without strengthening the résumé.

items.says: Consider whether the tools list omits tools you used and can support.
Name specific testing or performance tools you have used.
items.because: Some methods are broad, and specific tools may make the skills easier to evaluate.
